key_insight: A low-density, anisotropic triadic Fourier-space model still reproduces the hallmark 2D turbulence double cascade and Richardson pair superdiffusion.
engineering_relevance: This suggests reduced-order spectral models can capture key turbulent transport physics while using far fewer active interactions, useful for efficient simulation and analysis.
method: Sampled active resonant triads on ordered pseudo-logarithmic and disordered Fourier meshes
Varied angular sampling to tune anisotropy and triadic density
Evaluated Eulerian energy cascades and Lagrangian particle-pair dispersion
evidence_signal: Across all configurations, the model preserved a $k^{-5/3}$ inverse cascade, a $k^{-3}$ direct cascade, and pair separation scaling $?
watch_item: Spectral anisotropy changes vorticity organization and transport efficiency, so the dispersion amplitude and cascade strength may depend strongly on the chosen triad sampling.
paper_title: Exploring 2D turbulent properties in anisotropic and disordered Fourier space: Insights into inverse cascades and universal superdiffusion from randomly sampled triadic interaction
